claim: QA round 21 (#943 PARTIAL): a new device refused by the untrusted login buckets signs in with the emailed code, and that sign-in issues the same known-device token a password login gives (sign-in.controller.ts emailCodeVerify; EmailCodeVerifyDto declares signInDevice, max 512). The web client sends the token held for that email and keeps the one issued (services/api/passkeys.ts signInWithEmailCode), and the endpaper 429 note points to the emailed code instead of naming the connection.
verify: grep -q 'return { success: true, ...tokens, signInDevice };' apps/api-gateway/src/passkeys/sign-in.controller.ts && grep -q 'readSignInDevice(secret, dto.signInDevice, folded)' apps/api-gateway/src/passkeys/sign-in.controller.ts && grep -q 'signInDevice?: string;' apps/api-gateway/src/passkeys/dto/passkeys.dto.ts && grep -q 'rememberSignInDevice(email, data.signInDevice)' apps/web/src/services/api/passkeys.ts && grep -q 'email yourself a sign-in code below' apps/web/src/pages/Login.tsx && ! grep -q 'This connection has made too many sign-in attempts' apps/web/src/pages/Login.tsx
